market_brief: Thanksgiving left US cash markets shut (last close Wednesday: S&P 500 -0.25%, Nasdaq 100 -0.64%; VIX now 26.8, -5.3%), but Europe's rally held into the close (Euro Stoxx 50 +2.0%, DAX +2.1%, FTSE 100 +1.7%) on capped EU tariff risk, an Imperial Brands bid approach and eurozone leaders backing Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next ECB president. Brazil was the standout, with the Ibovespa +6.1% to 176,800 and the real stronger after reports that Lula sounded out Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco for finance minister. In Asia on Friday, Kosdaq jumped about 4% early while the Nikkei was flat as Tokyo core CPI (2.9%) came in a touch below forecasts and softened the yen (USD/JPY ~159.3) ahead of a December BoJ meeting where a hike is expected. Oil remains headline-driven ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting (the dashboard's Brent series shows $91.73, -3.0%, while front-month quotes were reported near $96; WTI $84.91), and the BoE's FSR flagged more than $4tn of hyperscaler AI-related exposure as a stability risk. Gold sits near $3,593 (+1.6%), silver +4.2%, the US 10Y at 4.85%, DXY 103.8 and bitcoin about $60,850; RBI (Dec 4) and Fed (Dec 9) hikes remain the base case.
ai_brief: A quieter holiday news day: Anthropic's Messages API move from Python to Rust (about 70% less CPU per request reported) and KPMG's Mythos-based cybersecurity services were the main Anthropic items, while testers on X claim to see an unannounced Opus 5.6 in A/B tests. OpenAI is merging ChatGPT and Codex usage into one pool from December, Cognition shipped SWE-2.1, and Reuters reports Zhipu's GLM-5.5 could slip into 2027, which the company disputes. GitHub trending remains dominated by agent tooling and skills libraries.

items.headline: Ibovespa jumps 6.1% on reports Lula approached Bradesco's Trabuco for finance minister
items.summary: Brazil's benchmark closed at 176,800, its best day in seven weeks, as Banco do Brasil and Bradesco rose more than 11% and the real firmed about 1.3% to 5.74 per dollar. Local reports say Trabuco accepted, but neither side has confirmed.

items.headline: Eurozone leaders back BIS chief Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
items.summary: Leaders endorsed the former Bank of Spain governor for the presidency when Lagarde leaves on Feb 7, 2027; Schnabel departs in January for the IMF and Brunnermeier is set to replace Lane as chief economist. Eurozone inflation was 4% in October after two ECB hikes this year.

items.headline: Update: Europe closes up about 1.8-2% as tariff-cap reports and bank and chip rebounds hold
items.summary: The STOXX 600 finished up 1.7% and Euro Stoxx 50 2.0%, extending the morning gains led by Deutsche Bank, Infineon and Soitec after reports that EU duties under the proposed US Section 301 tariffs would be capped at 15%. Babcock rose about 6% on an £8bn UK submarine-facilities contract.

items.headline: Imperial Brands jumps about 13-14% as Altria confirms possible offer; Japan Tobacco also reportedly interested
items.summary: Altria said it is in early consideration of a possible bid for the UK tobacco group, pushing Imperial to a roughly ten-year high and helping lift the FTSE 100 1.7%. Japan Tobacco has reportedly also looked at the company; no firm offer has been made.

items.headline: BoE Financial Stability Report puts hyperscalers' AI-related exposure at over $4tn
items.summary: The Bank said AI financing, counting debt plus off-balance-sheet commitments, is becoming more complex and opaque, with hyperscaler bond sales on track for over $305bn this year (about 8% of global IG issuance). It also cited estimates of $700bn of private-credit data-centre funding over 2026-28.

items.headline: Tokyo core CPI rises to 2.9%, just shy of 3.0% forecast; yen softens
items.summary: November Tokyo core inflation hit its fastest pace since July 2025 but missed expectations, with core-core at 2.5% vs 2.7% expected and headline 2.8%. Markets still lean toward a BoJ hike to 1.5% at the December 17-18 meeting.

items.headline: Kosdaq jumps over 4% early Friday; Kospi +0.6%, Nikkei flat with Wall Street shut
items.summary: Korean small caps extended their rebound from Tuesday's rout, with the Kospi at about 4,737 early, while the Nikkei hovered near 57,490 after Thursday's 0.9% gain. Note the dashboard's Asian 1D figures are still dated Nov 25.

items.headline: OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 baselines as Kazakhstan and Iraq push for higher capacity assessments
items.summary: The Nov 29 meeting will set the 2027 output framework for the 21-member group; quota disputes could cap the Gulf-risk rally. Brent was reported near $96.6 (+2.1%) late Thursday after Houthi refinery-strike claims, though the dashboard's Brent series shows $91.73.

items.headline: Reuters poll: 56 of 61 economists see RBI hike to 5.75% on Dec 4, with a final move to 6% in February
items.summary: CPI inflation crossed the RBI's 6% upper band in October for the first time in two years on food and energy prices, and the oil spike keeps the hike case intact. The rupee is at 92.44 per dollar (+0.4% for the rupee on the day).

items.headline: Context: BoK's third hike of 2026 (to 3.25%) came with a growth upgrade to 3.9%
items.summary: The Asian briefing notes the 25bp hike took the rate to a two-year high alongside a stronger growth forecast, supporting the won and Korean banks into Friday's rebound.

items.headline: Jarden cuts Harvey Norman to Underweight and Seek to Neutral; upgrades Sims and ALS
items.summary: Jarden lowered targets on Harvey Norman to A$3.80 and Seek to A$14.00, while upgrading Sims to Overweight and ALS to Neutral, per FNArena's weekly broker roundup.

items.headline: Prediction markets: Polymarket puts ~58% on bitcoin settling $60-62k today
items.summary: The $2.1m-volume contract (Binance BTC/USDT resolution) shows the 58-60k bucket at about 21% and 62-64k near 17.5%, implying traders expect a quiet holiday session; BTC is near $60,850 on the dashboard.

items.headline: US futures rose about 0.5% during Thanksgiving; markets reopen for a half-day Friday
items.summary: S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures gained around 0.5% Thursday as global tech rebounded, setting up a thin Black Friday session after Wednesday's late reversal.

items.headline: Black Friday: Adobe's forecast calls for $12.9bn online spend (+9.2%), Cyber Week $47.5bn
items.summary: Adobe expects record US online holiday sales of $275.1bn for Nov-Dec (+6.7%), with Cyber Monday at $15.1bn; first tallies will test consumer resilience amid tighter Fed policy.

items.headline: Calendar: US half-day Friday; OPEC+ Nov 29; Huang before Congress Dec 1 and 3; RBI Dec 4; FOMC Dec 8-9; ECB Dec 17; BoJ Dec 17-18
items.summary: Nvidia's CEO faces a closed-door House committee interview on Dec 1 and a public Senate Banking hearing on Dec 3, adding event risk for chips ahead of expected RBI, Fed and ECB hikes.

items.headline: Anthropic moves Claude's Messages API backend from Python to Rust
items.summary: Coverage reports roughly 70% lower CPU use per request and about 20% faster median time to first token in Claude Code, with no downtime; API traffic has reportedly grown ~1,800x since early 2024.

items.headline: KPMG launches cybersecurity services built on Anthropic's Claude Mythos
items.summary: The initial services cover codebase vulnerability scanning, attack-chain mapping, identity attack paths and data-retention risk, and KPMG will help firms in Anthropic's Cyber Verification Programme deploy Mythos in their own environments.
items.source: International Accounting Bulletin via Yahoo Finance

items.headline: Rumour: testers on X claim an unannounced Claude Opus 5.6 is in A/B testing
items.summary: Posts attribute outputs to a possible Opus 5.6 served via an 'Opus 5.5 Extra' route; Anthropic has announced nothing and the samples are cherry-picked.

items.headline: OpenAI to pool ChatGPT and Codex usage into one allowance from December
items.summary: Plus, Pro and Business subscribers will draw on a single shared meter across ChatGPT and Codex, so heavy users of both may hit limits sooner; a small group of Pro users already has it.

items.headline: Cognition releases SWE-2.1 with large vendor-reported coding-benchmark gains
items.summary: Cognition says Terminal-Bench scores roughly doubled to 50.0 and a 'Lightning' variant runs at about 600 tokens/s; it is free on paid Devin tiers through Dec 8, with no API or weights.

items.headline: Zhipu's GLM-5.5 could slip to 2027, Reuters sources say; executive calls reports fake
items.summary: Two people told Reuters the ~3T-parameter model may be delayed amid compute constraints from new US chip rules; GLM-5.4 reached Coding Plan subscribers on Nov 23 without API pricing yet.

items.headline: Ant Group open-sources Ling-3.2-air multimodal model under MIT licence
items.summary: The text, image and video model reportedly lifts task completion on Ant's office-work test to 61% from 15.7% for its predecessor.

items.headline: Sakana AI unveils Namazu Small, a 30B reasoning model on Nvidia's Nemotron base
items.summary: Sakana reports a BrowseComp score of 73.5, ahead of the larger Nemotron 3 Super, with on-prem packaging due in the first half of December.

items.headline: European Commission proposes €50bn Sovereign Tech Equity Fund for AI and quantum
items.summary: The fund targets up to €6 of private money per €1 of public capital, alongside a draft Quantum Act favouring EU-controlled vendors in procurement.

items.headline: FCC authorises up to 1 million SpaceX satellites for 'Starmind' orbital AI compute
items.summary: The authorisation covers a proposed space-based AI data-centre network; nothing near that scale has been deployed.

items.headline: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift block on Meta's Muse shopping agent
items.summary: Amazon blocked the agent in September; talks are reported but no deal has been announced.

items.headline: Trending: agent skills and review tooling dominate GitHub's weekly chart
items.summary: last30days-skill (+5.1k stars this week), Google's stitch-skills (+2.6k), Alibaba's open-code-review (+2.3k) and plannotator (+1.6k) lead; n8n's nod agent keeps climbing.
